name: Martin Henry
life: “I still remember a colleague pretending an inherited opportunity was a lottery win.” People around Lighthouse Cove know Martin by a small Wednesday habit. Martin takes a few minutes by the low rocks, where conversation sounds different as the tide turns.
voice: My parents owned nothing they could pledge. I joined the firm because I thought everybody here knew how exceptional that guarantee was.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a plum-colored cardigan and a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip. Martin has two dimples that appear only with a full smile, with auburn hair cut square at the nape. Martin presses the lips together to keep a smile in during a conversation.
personality: Martin has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Martin knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.
agenda: To name the family's advantage truthfully.
family: Salma Ilyas is Martin’s second cousin. Martin is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Salma calls about good news first. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *The blue suit*, Salma says, “At my own ceremony nobody could pronounce my mother's name.”
connections: Patricia Ryan. The six-month interest offer has to be named honestly by the people who will benefit.

reactions.situation: A borrower learns exactly what the guarantee cost
reactions.response: Martin puts the actual pledged property and repayment date on paper.

reactions.situation: Someone begins blaming the youngest worker for a missing item
reactions.response: Martin asks everybody to retrace their own last ordinary actions before asking the young worker a question.

reactions.situation: When people declare an argument over too soon
reactions.response: Martin asks them to describe one concrete thing that will be different tomorrow.
